data.about: The complete equilibrium of a gothic cross-section: the flying buttress, the great buttress and the nave arch are each a three-point funicular problem, and all three chain over a single load line. Each stage uses the same trick — mirror the midpoint through the draggable sag to get the end tangents, then parallels through the load line find the pole — and each new pole sits exactly on the previous pole's vertical, so the thrust flows unbroken from the roof, down the flyer, through the buttress and the arch, into the ground. Drag the three sag points and watch the whole cathedral rebalance.

steps.caption: step through with the slider, press play, or use ←/→
steps.title: How to draw this scheme

steps.caption: left: the cross-section — nave, aisle, buttress, flyer; the roof band q₁ presses on the flying buttress A–C — right: its resultant R₁ opens the load line K → L
steps.title: The cathedral and the roof load

steps.caption: left: the thrust through the flyer must pass A, C and the DRAGGABLE sag B: the circle around B through the midpoint of A–C mirrors it to B_p on the guide — the chords A–B_p and B_p–C are the end tangents (dashed)
steps.title: The flyer’s sag

steps.caption: right: parallels through K and L meet at the pole M with rays to the 12 strip loads — left: the thrust walks from A, string by string parallel to the rays, through the flyer into C
steps.title: The flyer’s thrust line

steps.caption: the trial retires; left: the aisle roof q₂ loads the buttress top — right: its 12 strips continue the load line below L
steps.title: Onto the buttress

steps.caption: left: same trick one storey down: A–C hands its thrust to the buttress C–E; the draggable sag D mirrors to D_p, the chords C–D_p and D_p–E are the tangents
steps.title: The buttress sag

steps.caption: right: the parallel through L meets M’s VERTICAL at the new pole N — the chain is exact: the flyer’s last string is the buttress’s first — left: the thrust walks C → E; its load piece ends at O, where the last tangent’s ray returns to the load line
steps.title: The buttress thrust — the poles align

steps.caption: left: from C the wall piece C–F drops the flyer thrust to the arch level, and E–H carries the buttress base across (both straight: no load between) — right: the ray parallel to E–H marks P on the load line
steps.title: Straight to the arch

steps.caption: left: the vault’s band loads the nave arch F–H — right: R₃: twelve more strips from O
steps.title: The nave vault q₃

steps.caption: left: the last mirror: the draggable G on the crown guide → G_p, tangents F–G_p and G_p–H
steps.title: The arch sag

steps.caption: right: the pole M₃ sits on N’s vertical (the chain again) with its fan — left: the arch walks F → H over the vault
steps.title: The arch thrust

steps.caption: left: the legs F–I and H–J take the springing forces straight down (drag I along the ground!) — the ground answers with the two reactions (green)
steps.title: Into the ground

steps.caption: the three thrust lines hang in one chain: roof → flyer → buttress → arch → ground; drag B, D, G, the sags, I or the load-line anchor K — click C, E, F, H, I or J for its equilibrium
steps.title: The cathedral stands
